Specifically the incentives for producing fraud proofs and possible attack vectors. In the papers I've seen, the subject is only treated very lightly, if at all. You're asking a leading question, which is a big no-no if you want to get to the truth! The verifier's dilemma only exists in academia. Thousands of full nodes are running for Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, etc., and all without direct in-protocol incentive. The incentives for verifying the rollup chain and producing fraud proofs really aren't complicated in practice. excerpts.author: jadler2664
excerpts.content:
You're asking a leading question, which is a big no-no if you want to get to the truth! The verifier's dilemma only exists in academia. Thousands of full nodes are running for Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, etc., and all without direct in-protocol incentive.

The incentives for verifying the rollup chain and producing fraud proofs really aren't complicated in practice. See section "Fast Withdrawals: Liquidity Providers" here: https://ethresear.ch/t/trustless-two-way-bridges-with-side-chains-by-halting/5728/
